question.worked_solution:
We proceed by setting the upper bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to \infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{2}^{\infty }\frac{12}{{y}^{4}}\,\text{d}y & ={lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{2}^{a}\frac{12}{{y}^{4}}\,\text{d}y \\  & =12{lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{2}^{a}{y}^{-4}\,\text{d}y \\  & =12{lim}_{a\to \infty }{[(-\frac{1}{3}{y}^{-3})]}_{2}^{a} \\  & =-4\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }{[\frac{1}{{y}^{3}}]}_{2}^{a} \\  & =-4\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }(\frac{1}{{a}^{3}}-\frac{1}{{2}^{3}}) \\  & =-4(0-\frac{1}{8}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
